finding.problem: A stale or alternate Forge writer can publish generic LIVE without proving it is the currently fused backlog-first executable.
finding.counterhypothesis: The writer may be a different current publisher rather than a stale process; exact executable/source/process identity distinguishes the cases.

delta.fail_closed: A writer whose entrypoint does not equal the committed Git blob, or whose process/supervisor generation cannot be bound, publishes state=RUNTIME_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED instead of inheriting LIVE.

cases: PID reuse is bound with Linux /proc start ticks
exact committed entrypoint produces VERIFIED identity
generic LIVE without runtime identity is rejected
exact live identity validates against current expected source

next_exact_gate: Fuse only after overlap review, then on the single authorized Forge supervisor path use the validator before accepting LIVE and require a fresh status whose exact source/process identity matches the expected backlog-first executable; runtime credit remains zero until that observed reconciliation executes.
evidence_boundary: The 5/5 local deterministic pass verifies helper logic only. It does not prove the live supervisor has restarted, that FORGE_LIVE is emitted by this branch, historical saturation, model/J-Space causality, training, full HCU, or whole EntityOS acceptance.
